records.title: Penumbra successor path evaluation
records.decision_rule: Preregister workload and platform thresholds before collection; require parity, material advantage, no lower-tier or native-backend regression, and acceptable maintenance.

records.title: Native backend entry and common-RHI parity
records.decision_rule: Metal first after stable contracts; Vulkan and D3D12 only after Metal differential, recovery, benchmark, divergence, staffing, and maintenance gates.

records.title: Artus motion-intent and negotiated-control contract
records.decision_rule: Preregister command and persistent-goal candidates, body-region arbitration, contact authority, interruption, replay, failure reporting, Cairn reconciliation, accessibility, security, and extension policy; adopt only a Meridian-owned contract with bounded deterministic and recoverable behavior.

records.title: Artus retargeting constraint pose-search and deformation portfolio
records.decision_rule: Compare retargeting, constraint solving, compression, pose-search, and CPU GPU deformation candidates against a preregistered humanoid corpus for correctness, recovery, determinism envelope, bounded cost, accessibility, security, licensing, provenance, and maintenance; preserve graph fallback and archive losing prototypes.

records.title: Meridian UI display-list renderer selection
records.decision_rule: ADR-0029 selects the Penumbra-owned direct display-list path from correctness, accessibility, integration, bounded-memory, platform, recovery, maintenance, and license evidence; performance and visual qualification remain package evidence rather than architecture selection claims.

records.title: Retained UI framework succession evaluation
records.decision_rule: Candidates are keep-Meridian-UI (baseline), and forks of Xilem/Masonry, Floem, and Vizia; GPUI is considered and rejected up front for Zed-coupling and pre-1.0 API instability rather than silently omitted. Stage one is a pass/fail precondition: a bounded spike renders Penumbra's live wgpu output inside a docked panel on each candidate; candidates that fail are cut before further evaluation. Stage two scores surviving candidates on performance, memory, accessibility proven by a real screen-reader pass, styling and extensibility depth, fork and vendoring maintenance burden, and weighted heaviest, how much of the existing meridian_ui_core/_semantics/_render/_text/_runtime behavior (reconciliation, focus-owning transient surfaces, accessibility command routing, the canonical workspaces, persistence and security boundary) is preserved unchanged versus rewritten against the candidate's own reactive model, plus continued conformance to the ui-design-tokens, ui-components, and ui-workspaces registries. Evidence is weighted toward independently reported field experience over each project's own documentation. No predetermined winner; retaining Meridian UI is a valid outcome, and a winning fork requires an explicit migration disposition for WP-UI-002 through WP-UI-006 plus a third_party/provenance/DEP-UI-* record before merge.

records.title: Cairn solver and determinism portfolio
records.decision_rule: Require provenance and differential corpus before migration; define measured determinism envelopes.

records.title: Isobar atmosphere and weather algorithms
records.decision_rule: Select per tier from visual, stability, determinism, cost, authorability, fallback, and coupling evidence.

records.title: Basalt geometry and terrain hierarchy
records.decision_rule: Select conventional LOD, meshlet, sparse, or hierarchy approaches by measured precision, streaming, deformation, memory, and maintenance.

records.title: Torsant specialized solver portfolio
records.decision_rule: Choose specialized optional solvers per effect/tier; no universal solver and no hidden disabled cost.

records.title: Alluvium evaluator representation and execution portfolio
records.decision_rule: Require a strict reference path; select scalar, SIMD, GPU, tiled, sparse, or worker kernels by structural correctness, determinism, latency, throughput, transfer, memory, recovery, platform coverage, debugging, and maintenance evidence.

records.title: Alluvium dependency replacement and deep kernel ownership
records.decision_rule: Keep permissive foundations by default; replacement requires preregistered material product benefit, representative evidence, provenance and license review, migration cost, maintainable ownership, and an ADR.

records.title: Release cryptography and key-management selection
records.decision_rule: Threat model, platform key storage, recovery, rotation, reproducibility, auditability, license, and maintenance decide.

records.title: Marquee local media audio and PDF adapter selection
records.decision_rule: Select mature local adapters by cross-platform coverage deterministic behavior licensing patent exposure sandboxability performance memory accessibility maintenance and escape-path evidence; do not presume custom Meridian codecs.

records.title: Competitive performance and quality comparison method
records.decision_rule: Preregister exact versions hardware profiles corpus settings warmup repetition statistics quality review workflow boundaries material thresholds expiration and retraction; promote only independently reproducible scoped claims with no lower-tier first-use memory recovery accessibility or maintenance regression.
